import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 289
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/289](https://www.erdosproblems.com/289)
-/

open Asymptotics Filter Finset

namespace Erdos289

/-- Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $k$, there exists finite intervals
$I_1, \dotsc, I_k \subset \mathbb{N}$ with $|I_i| \geq 2$ for $1 \leq i \leq k$ such that
$$
1 = \sum_{i=1}^k \sum_{n \in I_i} \frac{1}{n}.
$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_289 : answer(sorry) ↔
    (∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, ∃ I : Fin k → ℕ × ℕ,
    (∀ i, (I i).1 < (I i).2) ∧
    (∀ i j, i ≠ j → (I i).2 < (I j).1 ∨ (I j).2 < (I i).1) ∧
    ∑ i, ∑ n ∈ .Icc (I i).1 (I i).2, (n⁻¹ : ℚ) = 1) := by
  sorry

end Erdos289

findings.description: The separation condition on line 38 enforces disjointness but not non-adjacency. In particular, intervals [a,b] and [b+1,c] pass `(I i).2 < (I j).1`; the scratch file verifies this for [2,3] and [4,5]. The source explicitly prohibits adjacent intervals. Thus Lean permits adjacent pieces of one contiguous block to count separately toward k. Merging those pieces does not fix the discrepancy, because it decreases the prescribed number k of intervals.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/289 asks for all sufficiently large k for finite intervals I₁,…,Iₖ that are “distinct, not overlapping or adjacent,” each of cardinality at least 2, whose reciprocal sums total 1. The accompanying remark explains that these restrictions clarify the original Erdős–Graham wording.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the separation condition with `∀ i j, i ≠ j → (I i).2 + 1 < (I j).1 ∨ (I j).2 + 1 < (I i).1`. This requires at least one omitted natural number between distinct intervals.

findings.description: The theorem docstring on lines 28–32 omits all separation restrictions, including the pairwise disjointness already enforced by the Lean statement. It therefore describes the unrestricted problem allowing overlapping or repeated intervals, rather than either the Lean statement or the clarified problem on the cited page.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/289 explicitly requires distinct, non-overlapping, non-adjacent intervals and notes that the unrestricted original formulation is easily answered affirmatively by Kovac's argument. The mathematical argument appears at https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/289#post-665.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the docstring that the intervals are pairwise disjoint and non-adjacent, consistently with the clarified source and the corrected separation condition.

reformulations.difference: Using natural-number endpoints without explicitly requiring positive left endpoints admits zero denominators, unlike the ordinary reciprocal-sum interpretation. This domain difference is harmless for the eventual assertion, keeping the other conditions fixed.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For k ≥ 2, every interval with left endpoint strictly below its right endpoint has a strictly positive reciprocal sum. If one left endpoint were zero, that interval would contain 1 and contribute at least 1; another interval would contribute strictly positively, contradicting the total being 1. Therefore every solution for k ≥ 2 already has positive left endpoints. Restricting to k ≥ 2 does not change an atTop eventual assertion. The scratch theorem `Review289.eventually_positive_iff` proves the equivalence between the existing right-hand side and the same assertion with explicit positive left endpoints.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/289 — full statement, remarks, example, and OPEN status; retrieved through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/289 with HTML output.
https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/289#post-665 — mathematical argument and historical discussion in Kovac's 22 September 2025 comment.
https://www.erdosproblems.com/bibs/ErGr80 — bibliographic entry, retrieved through Jina.

P. Erdős and R. Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), pp. 33–34; https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf. Read using local OCR; printed page 34 is PDF page 30.
review.notes: Reviewed the sole declaration against the checklist and checked the answer machinery, interval/cardinality semantics, quantifiers, and reciprocal casts. `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` compiles without errors and contains the boundary tests and equivalence proofs; the positivity equivalence uses no sorry axioms. The target file remains unchanged. The historical book leaves separation unstated; the mathematical finding concerns the explicit clarified statement on the currently cited webpage. A source-forum grep incidentally surfaced a repository-specific comment; it was not pursued or used as evidence.

submission.summary: Strengthened the endpoint separation inequalities to require a missing natural number between distinct intervals, excluding adjacency. Updated the docstring to specify pairwise disjoint, non-adjacent intervals. The required Lean compilation succeeded with only the permitted `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
